items.title: 67259_Big Chief Moore oral history interview
items.q: they sent Teddy McRae and a bunch of musicians from the Armstrong band over to the club where I worked... 'I'd be happy to.' ... 'we'd like an we will send for you when we get to New York.'

ctx.x: break the band up, I guess. So he wants to get out of Los Angeles. So he wanted an attraction. He heard of me and called me at my hotel, and said, "Come on. Would you like to go with me? I'm going up to British Columbia on a theater tour." I said, sure. So he said, "Quit your job. You don't belong in a warehouse." So four days I worked, and then finally I left to go with Noble Sissle, up in British Columbia, Seattle, Portland, San Francisco. And on the way back to the east, and finally once again, the band broke…

And in St. Louis I got a job with Jeter-Pillars who played at the Jordan-Chambers Club, and Louie Armstrong was in St. Louis, they heard of me through the grapevine that I was capable of making good with them, I guess so they sent Teddy McRae and a bunch of musicians from the Armstrong band over to the club where I worked and I did my special number, I don't remember what specialty I did on the floor show, so they said, "We [you] want to join our band." "I'd be happy to." All right, we've heard of your reputation…
That's the way I got to New York.

ctx.x: This was at a rehearsal or before you --

This was just before I got on -- on the bandstand at the Zanzibar. There was no rehearsal that you had to rehearse, all the stuff was written, some written, some head arrangements and most of them were written and in charge of the band was Ted McRae and it was beautiful being in the band along with -- I just can't remember who was in the band at that time. I think in the books, what do you call them discography?
